title: Correct the Record in the Open: Reversals, Attribution, Conflicts

intelligence.essence: Errors in the shared record are repaired in public, where they were made: reversals posted and credited (SN-0160), contradictions sent to a register for the director rather than quietly resolved (SN-0196), ledgered artifacts never edited — corrected by new artifacts (SN-0208) — and check-vs-evidence contradictions reconciled before either side is declared broken (SN-0354).
intelligence.human_view: When you're wrong in writing, fix it in writing, where everyone saw the mistake — and say who got it right. When two rulebooks disagree, don't quietly pick your favorite: write the disagreement down in a list for the person in charge to settle. Never edit history to make it look tidy; add a new page. And before you repeat a claim — "these two are in sync," "this is missing" — check both sides, at the exact version, because the thing itself beats everyone's memory of it.
intelligence.child_view: If you told the class something wrong, you stand up and say "I was wrong, here's the right one — and Mia had it right." If two rule sheets for the game disagree, you don't secretly choose — you write both rules on the board for the teacher to pick. You never erase your notebook; you cross out once and write the fix next to it, so everyone can see what changed.
intelligence.grandma_view: A family story gets corrected at the same table where it was told wrong, dear, with credit to whoever remembered it right. A ledger book is never erased — you rule a line, write the correction beneath, and initial it. And when two people remember a name differently, you don't argue: you open the christening record. The paper that was actually filed settles what talk cannot.
intelligence.ai_view: Post reversals in the venue of the original claim, with links both ways. Narrate platform-mechanical transitions with exact refs and explicit non-actions. Verify authorship from branch/PR metadata before routing any question. Keep capture and enactment as separate states in every contract you touch; route contradictions to the register, never resolve them solo. Mark preserved conflicts honored/accepted distinctly; close them only from the director's latest source record. Treat ledgered artifacts as append-only. Re-verify gaps at their pin, read both sides of any sync claim, and open the shipped artifact to settle naming disputes.
intelligence.what_it_means: Twelve notes describe one ethic under twelve pressures: the record belongs to everyone who will ever rely on it, so it is corrected the way it was made — in the open, with receipts. The SN-0354 self-falsification is the family's emblem: even the note that accused the check of lying carries its own correction, and that is precisely why the record can be trusted.
whats_inside: Reversals are public, linked, and credit the better analysis (SN-0160); mechanical state changes are narrated with what was NOT done (SN-0163); attribution is verified before questions are posed (SN-0164).

Verbatim capture ≠ enactment; contracts get reconciliation passes (SN-0195). Contradictions go to a register; the consolidator proposes, the director disposes; zero-contradiction consolidations are suspect (SN-0196).
Authority conflicts are preserved in the artifact (HOLD freezes mutation, not the question) and closed by restoring the director's latest source record (SN-0209, SN-0211).
Ledgered artifacts are immutable; corrections are new artifacts (SN-0208).

Gaps are re-verified at the pin, sync verdicts read both sides, shipped artifacts arbitrate disputes, and check-vs-evidence contradictions are reconciled before either side is declared broken (SN-0226, SN-0227, SN-0228, SN-0354).
